title: Lessons with Santo Giuffre, Eddie Miller and a musical family
summary: Studied with Giuffre, taught Eddie Miller what he learned, and later taught Giuffre saxophone; mother and sisters were musical; Giuffre's solfege training.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: It seems like as though I came up just during the shift, just before the shift to the BAME you see. And I was playing for about three years and I decided to learn how to read music so I went to an old Professor Giuffre here.
Oh I've heard of him. What was his name, Santo?

Santo Giuffre. He was a very, very fine musician, very good teacher. And Eddie Miller and I started together and Eddie was always broke. So I'd go take a lesson and Eddie would meet me at my house and I'd teach him what the professor taught me. So Eddie calls me Professor today.
That's funny. So he's about your age?
Eddie is about three years younger than I am, approximately.
Let me see now. We were talking about your family. You said your sister studied piano and voice. Anybody else in your family musical at all?

Well, no, not too much. My mother had quite a nice operatic voice, a soprano voice, but she never would do anything with it. And the others, a couple of my sisters played piano. One of them used to fake play anything she wanted by ear, you know. She wouldn't take the trouble to study music. But then I went to Giuffre for a couple of years and everything I did I did wrong naturally. Had to learn how to play all over again. And I taught him how to play a saxophone. Is that right? Because he was playing at the Orphan Theater then and they told him he'd have to play saxophone. He didn't know the first thing about it. So one day he went for my lesson and he said, can you teach me how to play saxophone? So I did the best I could.
That wasn't hard I imagine families make that switch.

No, no. He taught solfeggio you know. And he could recite solfeggio fast and you could execute on an instrument. The guy was fabulous. He played with a lot of the great big symphonies around the country. He was from Milan, Italy. And he told me that he wanted to study violin. But in an old country like that you don't study what you want, you study what they think you're better suited for. So they started him on clarinet. And incidentally he told me that he had gone to school or to music school for several years before they ever let him touch an instrument. Just learn the music you know. Fazolo would start that way too. Learn solfeggio before he ever played.
